entry.title: SQL Server Myth: “Checkpoint Only Writes Pages from Committed Transactions”
entry.summary: Checkpoints in SQL Server are often misunderstood. Contrary to popular belief, they don’t only flush committed data they write all dirty pages, even from uncommitted transactions. Transactional safety comes from the log and recovery process, not from checkpoint filtering.

entry.title: LLM and SLM collaboration using the Minions pattern (with Phi-4-mini and Azure OpenAI)
entry.summary: In this post, we’ll explore a novel approach to optimizing AI workflows by strategically combining large language models (LLMs) with small language models (SLMs) using the “Minions pattern.” This technique, described in the research paper “Minions: Cost-efficient Collaboration Between On-device and Cloud Language Models” by Narayan et al., addresses one of the most pressing challenges in AI application development - the cost of processing large amounts of data with expensive, cloud-based language models. If you’ve ever built an AI system that needs to analyze extensive documents or datasets, you’ve probably felt the frustration of watching your API costs skyrocket as you process more and more content.
